routes.name: Atlantic triangle, leg 1: Liverpool to the Bight of Biafra
citations: Eric Williams, Capitalism and Slavery (Chapel Hill: University of North Carolina Press, 1944)
Olaudah Equiano, The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano (London, 1789) [public domain]
routes.notes: British slaving voyages carried trade goods to West Africa to buy captives. Shown from 1700 to the British abolition of the trade in 1807; other nations' trade ran earlier and later.
routes.goods_source: general history; not from a cargo manifest
routes.citation: Eric Williams, Capitalism and Slavery (Chapel Hill: University of North Carolina Press, 1944)

routes.name: Atlantic triangle, leg 2: the Middle Passage
goods: enslaved African people, transported by force
citations: Olaudah Equiano, The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano (London, 1789) [public domain]
Marcus Rediker, The Slave Ship: A Human History (New York: Viking, 2007)
routes.notes: Captive Africans were shipped across the Atlantic in brutal conditions; many died on the voyage. Equiano, who survived it as a child, wrote one of the few first-hand accounts. Shown factually, with no game-like effects.
routes.citation: Olaudah Equiano, The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano (London, 1789) [public domain]
